d: A Python framework for connecting LLMs to your data through ingestion, indexing, retrieval, agents and event-driven workflows.
x: LlamaIndex specializes in data ingestion, indexing and retrieval for LLM apps.

d: The core package containing LlamaIndex's base abstractions such as indexes, retrievers, query engines and Settings.
x: Integrations are installed as separate llama-index-* packages on top of llama-index-core.

d: The registry of community integrations: data readers, tools, vector stores and more.
x: LlamaHub hosts hundreds of data connectors.

d: LlamaIndex's document parsing service that converts complex PDFs with tables and layouts into clean Markdown or JSON.
x: LlamaParse can return results as Markdown.

d: A container for a data source (file, page, row) with text and metadata.
c: Document(text="LlamaIndex connects LLMs to data.", metadata={"source": "intro.md"})
x: A Document can carry metadata such as source and year.

d: A chunk of a Document — the atomic unit that is embedded and retrieved, with metadata and relationships.
c:
from llama_index.core.schema import TextNode
TextNode(text="a chunk", metadata={"page": 3})
x: Nodes keep relationships such as their source document and previous/next node.

d: Built-in reader that loads files from a directory, handling PDF, DOCX, Markdown, CSV and more.
x: required_exts limits which file extensions are loaded.

d: Node setting that hides certain metadata keys from the text used for embedding.
x: Metadata can be shown to the LLM but excluded from the embedding text.

d: Restricting retrieval to nodes whose metadata matches conditions such as year >= 2026.
x: MetadataFilters can be passed to as_retriever(filters=...).

d: The default node parser that creates token-sized chunks while respecting sentence boundaries.
x: SentenceSplitter takes chunk_size and chunk_overlap arguments.

d: Node parser that splits text where embedding similarity between adjacent sentences drops.
x: Semantic splitting requires an embedding model.

d: Parser that creates one node per sentence and stores the surrounding sentences as a window in metadata.
x: It is used together with MetadataReplacementPostProcessor.

d: Parser that creates parent and child nodes at several chunk sizes, e.g. 2048, 512 and 128.
x: Hierarchical nodes enable auto-merging retrieval.

d: Structure-aware parser that splits Markdown by headings.
x: MarkdownNodeParser keeps document structure when splitting Markdown.

d: Language-aware splitter that chunks source code along syntactic boundaries.
x: CodeSplitter takes a language argument such as "python".

d: A global singleton of defaults such as the LLM, embedding model and chunk size.
x: Components passed explicitly override the global Settings.

d: Chains transformations (splitters, extractors, embeddings) with caching, de-duplication and optional vector-store writes.
c:
pipeline = IngestionPipeline(transformations=[SentenceSplitter(), TitleExtractor(), OpenAIEmbedding()], vector_store=vs, docstore=docstore)
nodes = pipeline.run(documents=docs)
x: Attaching a docstore enables de-duplication and upserts of changed documents.

d: Transformations such as TitleExtractor and KeywordExtractor that use an LLM to add metadata to nodes.
x: TitleExtractor adds an LLM-generated title to node metadata.

d: Cache of (node, transformation) results so unchanged data is not re-processed.
x: Re-running a pipeline with the cache skips work already done.

d: The workhorse index that embeds nodes and retrieves the top-k most similar ones.
x: VectorStoreIndex.from_documents splits, embeds and stores documents in one call.

d: Index that returns all nodes (optionally filtered), suited to summarising whole documents.
x: SummaryIndex is typically paired with tree_summarize synthesis.

d: Index that builds a hierarchy of summaries and traverses it top-down at query time.
x: TreeIndex organizes nodes into a tree of summaries.

d: Index that maps extracted keywords to nodes for keyword-based lookup.
x: KeywordTableIndex retrieves nodes whose keywords match the query.

d: Index that builds a knowledge graph of entities and relations (plus vectors) for graph-based retrieval.
x: PropertyGraphIndex uses kg_extractors such as SimpleLLMPathExtractor.

d: Graph extractor that restricts extracted entities and relations to an allowed schema.
x: A schema produces cleaner, more consistent graphs than free-form extraction.

d: Index storing a summary per document to pick relevant documents before retrieving their chunks.
x: DocumentSummaryIndex helps route queries across many documents.

d: Bundle of the docstore, index store, vector store and graph store used by an index.
x: StorageContext.from_defaults(vector_store=vs) plugs an external vector DB into an index.

d: Saves an index's storage (docstore, index store, vectors) to a directory.
x: index.storage_context.persist(persist_dir="./storage") writes the index to disk.

d: Rebuilds an index from a persisted StorageContext without re-embedding.
x: load_index_from_storage needs a StorageContext created from the persist directory.

d: Creates a VectorStoreIndex on top of an existing populated vector store.
x: VectorStoreIndex.from_vector_store(vs) reuses vectors already stored in the DB.

d: An end-to-end question-answering interface combining a retriever, node postprocessors and a response synthesizer.
x: index.as_query_engine() returns a query engine with default components.

d: Component that returns the most relevant nodes (with scores) for a query, without generating an answer.
x: retriever.retrieve(q) returns a list of NodeWithScore.

d: Parameter controlling how many top-scoring nodes a vector retriever returns.
x: similarity_top_k=5 returns at most five nodes.

d: A retrieved node paired with its relevance score.
c:
for n in nodes:
    print(n.score, n.node.metadata)
x: Each retrieved result exposes .node and .score.

d: Node postprocessor that drops retrieved nodes whose score is below a cutoff.
x: SimilarityPostprocessor(similarity_cutoff=0.75) removes nodes scoring below 0.75.

d: Postprocessor that re-ranks retrieved nodes with a cross-encoder and keeps the top_n.
x: Rerankers are applied after retrieval, typically keeping fewer nodes (top_n).

d: Postprocessor that uses an LLM to select and order the most relevant retrieved nodes.
x: LLMRerank is more expensive than a cross-encoder reranker.

d: Postprocessor that replaces a node's text with a metadata field, such as its sentence window.
x: It is the second half of sentence-window retrieval.

d: Postprocessor that places the most relevant nodes at the start and end of the context to counter "lost in the middle".
x: LongContextReorder changes node order, not node content.

d: The default synthesis mode that packs as many chunks as fit into each LLM call and refines across calls.
x: compact makes fewer LLM calls than refine for the same chunks.

d: Synthesis mode that makes one LLM call per chunk, iteratively refining the answer.
x: refine with 6 retrieved chunks makes about 6 LLM calls.

d: Synthesis mode that summarizes chunks recursively bottom-up into a final answer.
x: tree_summarize is well suited to summarization queries.

d: Synthesis mode that returns retrieved nodes without calling the LLM.
x: no_text is useful to inspect retrieval results only.

d: The retrieved nodes attached to a response, used for citations.
x: response.source_nodes lists the nodes used to build the answer.

d: Query engine where an LLM selector chooses the best underlying engine for each query.
x: RouterQueryEngine uses a selector to pick among query engine tools.

d: Query engine that decomposes a complex question into sub-questions over different tools, then combines the answers.
x: Each sub-question is answered by a query engine tool before the final synthesis.

d: Retriever that merges retrieved child nodes into their parent when enough siblings are retrieved.
x: AutoMergingRetriever works with nodes from a HierarchicalNodeParser.

d: A stateful, multi-turn interface that adds conversation history to retrieval.
x: chat_engine.reset() clears the conversation memory.

d: Chat mode that rewrites a follow-up into a standalone question before querying the index.
x: condense_question uses chat history to rewrite the latest message.

d: Chat mode that condenses the question, retrieves context, then answers with both history and context.
x: condense_plus_context combines question condensing with retrieved context.

d: Chat mode that retrieves with the user message and places the context in the system prompt.
x: context mode retrieves on every user message.

d: Component that keeps recent chat messages within a token limit and can maintain long-term memory blocks.
x: Memory.from_defaults(token_limit=...) bounds how much history is kept.

d: Chat engine method that streams the answer token by token.
x: stream_chat returns a response whose response_gen yields tokens.

d: Tool wrapper that turns a Python function into an agent tool using its signature and docstring.
x: Plain functions passed to agents are converted into FunctionTools automatically.

d: Tool that exposes a query engine (RAG pipeline) to an agent with a name and description.
x: The tool description tells the agent when to use the query engine.

d: Agent that uses the LLM's native function/tool-calling API to choose and call tools.
c:
agent = FunctionAgent(tools=[multiply, docs_tool], llm=llm, system_prompt="Use tools.")
response = await agent.run(user_msg="What is 12 * 4?")
x: FunctionAgent requires an LLM with function-calling support.

d: Agent that reasons with prompted Thought/Action/Observation steps and works with any LLM.
x: ReActAgent does not require native function calling.

d: Agent that writes and executes code as its action.
x: CodeActAgent's actions are code snippets that must be executed safely.

d: Multi-agent orchestration where agents hand off control to each other, starting from a root agent.
c:
workflow = AgentWorkflow(agents=[research, writer], root_agent="Researcher")
await workflow.run(user_msg="Report on GraphRAG")
x: can_handoff_to restricts which agents an agent may hand off to.

d: The workflow Context object that carries agent state and memory across runs.
c:
ctx = Context(agent)
await agent.run(user_msg="My name is Meera", ctx=ctx)
x: Passing the same ctx to agent.run keeps conversation state.

d: Events like AgentStream, ToolCall, ToolCallResult and AgentOutput emitted while an agent runs.
c:
handler = agent.run(user_msg="...")
async for ev in handler.stream_events():
    print(type(ev).__name__)
x: Streaming events lets a UI show tool calls as they happen.

d: An event-driven class whose @step methods consume and emit typed events from StartEvent to StopEvent.
x: Agents in LlamaIndex are built on Workflows.

d: Decorator marking a workflow method as a step; its type annotations define the events it accepts and returns.
c:
@step
async def synthesize(self, ctx: Context, ev: RetrievedEvent) -> StopEvent: ...
x: The event type in a step's signature determines which events trigger it.

d: The event that begins a workflow, carrying the keyword arguments passed to run().
c:
async def first(self, ev: StartEvent) -> MyEvent:
    q = ev.query
x: wf.run(query="x") makes ev.query available on the StartEvent.

d: The event that ends a workflow; its result is returned from run().
x: Returning StopEvent(result=x) makes run() return x.

d: A user-defined subclass of Event carrying typed fields between steps.
x: Custom events are Pydantic-style classes with typed fields.

d: Workflow Context storage for sharing state across steps with set and get.
c:
await ctx.store.set("query", ev.query)
query = await ctx.store.get("query")
x: await ctx.store.set("query", q) makes the value available to later steps.

d: Context method to emit events manually, e.g. to fan out many parallel events.
x: send_event can emit several events to trigger parallel processing.

d: Context method that waits until a set of events has arrived before continuing (fan-in).
x: collect_events returns None until all expected events are buffered.

d: Context method that publishes progress events to the caller's stream.
x: The caller can read these events via handler.stream_events().

d: Step option allowing several events to be processed by the same step concurrently.
c:
@step(num_workers=4)
async def grade(self, ev: GradeEvent) -> GradeResult: ...
x: @step(num_workers=4) can process four events in parallel.

d: Constructor argument that limits how long a workflow run may take.
x: Workflow(timeout=60) raises an error if the run exceeds 60 seconds.

d: The standalone package for Workflows, usable outside the rest of LlamaIndex.
c:
from workflows import Workflow, step, Context
from workflows.events import StartEvent, StopEvent
x: Workflows can be imported from the standalone workflows package.

d: LLM-based evaluator checking whether a response is supported by the retrieved context.
x: FaithfulnessEvaluator returns passing, score and feedback.

d: Evaluator checking whether the response and retrieved context are relevant to the query.
x: RelevancyEvaluator considers the query, context and response.

d: Evaluator that scores a response against a reference answer on a 1–5 scale.
x: CorrectnessEvaluator needs a reference answer.

d: Evaluator computing retrieval metrics like hit rate and MRR over question-context pairs.
x: RetrieverEvaluator.from_metric_names(["hit_rate", "mrr"], retriever=r) builds the evaluator.

d: Utility that uses an LLM to create synthetic questions for each node, producing a retrieval eval dataset.
x: The generated dataset maps questions to the nodes that answer them.

d: Fraction of queries whose relevant chunk appears in the top-k results.
c: hit_rate = sum(rel in top_k for rel, top_k in results) / len(results)
x: Hit rate ignores the exact position as long as the relevant chunk is in the top k.

d: Mean reciprocal rank: the average of 1/rank of the first relevant result per query.
c: mrr = sum(1 / rank for rank in first_relevant_ranks) / len(first_relevant_ranks)
x: A relevant result at rank 2 contributes 0.5 to the MRR average.

d: LlamaIndex's built-in system emitting events and spans that observability tools consume.
x: OpenInference's LlamaIndexInstrumentor hooks into LlamaIndex instrumentation.
